title.narrative: Provision of vital WASH support to vulnerable drought- and conflict-affected populations in Bosasso, Puntland, Somalia.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtPuntland Minority Women Development Organization (PMWDO) proposes to implement WASH interventions in Bosaso District, Puntland, as part of a life-saving emergency response aligned with the 2025 Somalia Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) and the OCHA SHF Drought Allocation Strategy for Northern Somalia. The project aims to provide safe water services to approximately 27,000 drought- and conflict-affected individuals living in rural villages and IDP settlements, including Jeedaal, Jiingada, Wardheer, Laag, Kalabeyr, Laasadawaco, Geesaqabad, Yalho, Seylada Xoolaha, Ajuuraan, Biyo Kulule, and Wadajir zone.ltbrgtThese communities face severe water shortages and an increased risk of waterborne diseases due to recurrent drought conditions and population displacement. To address these urgent needs, PMWDO will rehabilitate four boreholes located in Carmo, Jiingada, Wardheer, and Wadajir IDP, and drill two new boreholes in Geesaaqabad and Laasadawaco village. The project will also extend piped water networks and construct 13 communal water kiosks to enhance equitable water access across target locations. Emergency water trucking will be provided, along with water treatment and chlorination in AWD/Cholera-prone areas.ltbrgtImportantly, all infrastructure developed through this project will be handed over to trained WASH committees within the local community, ensuring sustainable management and operation. This process will be supported by a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Puntland Water Development Agency. The project will also take into consideration the specific needs of people with disabilities to ensure their equitable access to water services. This integrated WASH response, implemented over 10 months, will target 4,500 households (27,000 individuals), directly reducing health risks, enhancing water safety, and improving dignity and resilience among the most vulnerable populations in Bosaso District.ltbrgtlt/pgt
